subject: APAC peering partition: customer action + recovery summary
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@acme.example.com>, Acme Platform Ops <ops@acme.example.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 01:12:00 +0000
Subject: APAC peering partition — immediate reroute recommendation

Elaine / Acme ops team,

Quick update and recommended immediate action. We observed a regional peering partition affecting a subset of APAC fabric (apac-1) starting ~2028-01-15 00:40 UTC. Symptoms: elevated latencies (tail > 3s for generation), intermittent 502/504 errors for private deployments with APAC endpoints, and failed KV cache reconciliation for a small percentage of Dedicated pods.

Impact summary:
- Scope: Customers on apac-1 endpoints (Private & Dedicated) — traffic hitting apac-1 may experience errors or increased latency.
- Estimated affected percentage: ~7% of tokens served to APAC header traffic at peak.
- No user data loss observed; all persisted logs intact.

Immediate recommendation (action required on your side):
1) Update your Redwood endpoint to the temporary APAC-fallback host: apac-fallback.rw-inference.com (CNAME to eu-west-1/ us-east-1 based on routing policy).
2) If you manage DNS TTLs: lower TTL to 60s for the redispatch window, then restore after 24 hours.
3) If you use static host bindings, switch to the alternate host in your env vars and restart the service replica (example below).

Sample curl for testing (no auth token shown):
curl -X POST https://apac-fallback.rw-inference.com/v1/generate
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"healthcheck"}'

We've attached a short playbook (apac_reroute_playbook.pdf) with step-by-step DNS and SDK changes plus rollback instructions. Our infra team is implementing provider-level mitigations and will push an automated fallback for Dedicated pools where possible.

We realize this is disruptive — we are treating this as a high-severity incident and will follow up with a compact postmortem and proposed credits. Please reply with a preferred contact and best time if you want a quick 15-min bridge.

— Priyom

Thanks Priyom — we see the same in our metrics. High-level questions:
- Can you confirm whether existing KV cache entries will be invalidated after the switch? We saw some repeated cold-starts this morning.
- What is the expected latency delta if we route to eu-west-1? Our SLOs target median <200ms for inference in APAC regions.

Ops note: our DNS is managed by Platform; we can lower TTL now and plan to flip at 02:00 UTC if you confirm the fallback is stable.

Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 01:48:05 +0000
Subject: Re: APAC peering partition — immediate reroute recommendation

Hi Elaine — brief technical clarifications and guidance.

1) KV cache behavior: switching endpoints will direct requests to a different worker pool; existing in-memory KV caches on apac-1 nodes will not be immediately available after cutover. For most request patterns you'll see cache-miss cold starts for the first few minutes per client. We recommend a steady rollout (traffic shifting over a few minutes) rather than a hard cut to reduce cold-start amplification. Persistent storage/backing store remains intact; no persistent keys were lost.

2) Latency expectations to eu-west-1: median increase is typically ~70–120ms extra RTT from major APAC metros (Singapore, Tokyo). We estimate median ~280–320ms for inference + network with the eu fallback; token-level generation cost will not increase. If you require <200ms median, the fallback will degrade that target.

3) Proposed operational plan (we can execute with you):
- 02:00 UTC: Lower TTL to 60s (Ops).
- 02:05–02:10 UTC: Gradual CNAME switch to apac-fallback.rw-inference.com (start with 10% traffic).
- 02:10–02:25 UTC: Ramp to 100% if error rates decline.
- 02:30 UTC: Confirm traffic stabilization; begin TTL restoration.

CLI sample to rotate host (node restart not required for SDKs that resolve DNS each request):
export REDWOOD_HOST=https://apac-fallback.rw-inference.com
# test
curl -v $REDWOOD_HOST/v1/health

We will remain on the bridge and push updates to this thread. Attachment contains a checklist and rollback commands.

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Product Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Attachment: apac_reroute_playbook.pdf

Date: Mon, 16 Jan 2028 08:10:30 +0000
Subject: APAC peering partition — mitigation update

Elaine,
Quick operational update following yesterday's changes: we applied the controlled CNAME shift at 02:07 UTC with the ramp plan Vanessa outlined. Observations:
- Error rates for your tenant dropped to baseline within ~12 minutes of the 10%->100% ramp.
- Cold-starts observed but mostly within the first 3 requests per client; cache warmup completed within ~6–9 minutes for typical traffic patterns.
- We applied an automated dedicated-pool fallback for eligible Dedicated customers; for your Dedicated instances we saw connection handoffs complete gracefully.

Next: we will keep the fallback host active for 72 hours while the cloud provider stabilizes peering. Please continue to monitor and let us know if you see any residual 5xx errors. If you want us to automate the change permanently we can begin a controlled traffic-shift to eu-backend for a longer window, but that requires a short config change and your approval.

Thanks for the fast coordination and apologies for the disruption — we're preparing a short post-incident summary and a credit offer for impacted usage.

— Priyom
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@acme.example.com>, Acme Platform Ops <ops@acme.example.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident summary — APAC peering partition (Jan 15–16 2028)

Elaine / Acme ops,

Attached is our compact post-incident summary (postmortem_summary_20280118.pdf). Key items in the body below.

Timeline (condensed):
- 2028-01-15 00:40 UTC: Onset of peering partition affecting apac-1 (CloudZone report of route flap).
- 2028-01-15 01:12 UTC: Redwood customer ops notified (this thread).
- 2028-01-15 02:07 UTC: Controlled CNAME reroute executed (apac-fallback).
- 2028-01-15 02:20 UTC: Error rates returned to baseline for Acme tenant.
- 2028-01-16 08:00 UTC: Automated Dedicated fallback applied for eligible pools.

Root cause: an inter-provider peering flap at CloudZone in apac-1 that caused asymmetric routing to a subset of our worker subnets. The flap triggered session drops and transient TCP resets manifesting as 502/504 for in-flight requests.

What we did:
- Coordinated directly with CloudZone operations to patch route advertisements and stabilize the fabric.
- Implemented an automated CNAME-based fallback routing that can be enabled for any APAC tenant within minutes.
- For Dedicated: added a quick-handoff path that preserves session affinity where possible.

Customer-facing remediation and next steps:
- We are issuing a usage credit for impacted requests between 2028-01-15 00:40 UTC and 2028-01-16 08:00 UTC. See customer_credit_agreement.docx attached — sign and we will apply.
- We have a permanent mitigation plan: (1) expanded multi-path peering for APAC regions, (2) improved health-detection and automated reroute thresholds, (3) SDK-level graceful retry guidance published in next week.

Action items for Acme (recommended but optional):
- Confirm acceptance of credit agreement and preferred method for applying credit (invoicing vs. usage credit).
- If <200ms median is a hard requirement, let's plan a deeper discussion on architecture options (edge proxy + local inference, or hybrid model).

Again — sincere apologies for the disruption. We recognize the impact on your service and are committed to preventing recurrence. I (Markus) will lead the post-incident review and would be happy to walk through the attached summary and answer questions on a short call.

— Markus Klein
VP, Production Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Attachment: postmortem_summary_20280118.pdf; customer_credit_agreement.docx
